newsitem.title: SPAIN: U.S. criticises Telefonica Latam monopolies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. criticises Telefonica Latam monopolies.

text.p: Mindel De la Torre, director of U.S. telecommunications regulator Federal Communications Commission (FCC), criticised Telefonica's monopolies in Latin America in an interview with Expansion on Monday.
"The FCC would be pleased if there were competition in the markets of Argentina and Peru," De La Torre told the financial daily.
The international arm of Spain's Telefonica, TISA, controls units that operate a monopoly in basic telephone services, although in Argentina, TASA controls only half of the country.

"We would like to see competition as soon as possible. We believe the operators don't need a monopoly. Telefonica doesn't need a monopoly for five years -- until May 1999 -- like the one it will have in Peru on basic telephone services," De la Torre said.
But the director of the FCC called Chile, where Telefonica controls the principal operator CTC, a model of success, whose opening to competition prompted a strong fall in tariffs.

With respect to Spain's telecommunications, De La Torre said that the decision to move the liberalisation forward to December 1998 was well received in the U.S., although it added that the final objective is that the market is liberalised in January 1998.
